title: Electricity sources in Danmoor
prompt: The pie charts show the proportion of electricity generated from five different sources in the country of Danmoor in 1995, 2005 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Electricity generated by source, Danmoor, 1995, 2005 and 2020

sentences.text: The pie charts compare the share of electricity that Danmoor produced from five energy sources in 1995, 2005 and 2020.
sentences.why: Paraphrases without copying: "compare" replaces "show", "share" replaces "proportion" and "produced" replaces "generated". It states the three years, so the introduction earns Task Achievement and shows Lexical Resource with no data added.

sentences.text: Overall, coal changed from being the dominant source of electricity to a minor one, while renewables followed the opposite pattern.
sentences.why: A clear overview of the biggest shift across the three pies. "Dominant" and "minor" rank the sources without numbers, and "the opposite pattern" links two items. This secures the key Task Achievement requirement.

sentences.text: The other three sources were far more stable, although gas gained ground gradually.
sentences.why: The second overview feature contrasts stability with change, which shows selection. "Far more stable" and "gained ground" paraphrase trend language and avoid figures, supporting Task Achievement and Lexical Resource at the overview stage.

sentences.text: Coal and renewables moved in opposite directions over the 25 years.
sentences.why: A topic sentence that groups the two sources by their shared story. "In opposite directions" frames the paragraph before any figures, earning Coherence and Cohesion, and "over the 25 years" fixes the time span accurately.

sentences.text: Coal supplied 48 per cent of electricity in 1995, but this fell to 36 per cent in 2005 and to just 9 per cent in 2020.
sentences.why: Gives the three exact coal values in sequence with correct units. "Supplied" varies the verb for share, "just" signals how small 9 per cent is, and the sentence shows accurate Task Achievement and Grammatical Range.

sentences.text: Renewables, by contrast, began as the smallest source, at only 3 per cent, before rising to 7 per cent and then to 36 per cent.
sentences.why: Contrasts renewables with coal using "by contrast". The chain "began as", "rising to" and "then to" reports all three pie values efficiently, showing range of structures and accurate trend data for Task Achievement.

sentences.text: As a result, renewables had become the largest source by 2020, having replaced coal in that position.
sentences.why: "Having replaced" is a perfect participle clause that links the two trends into one rank change. This is the insight a pie report needs beyond reading values, and it supports Coherence and Grammatical Range.

sentences.text: The remaining three sources were considerably steadier.
sentences.why: A short topic sentence that introduces the second group and signals a contrast with Body 1 through "steadier". It organises the report by meaning rather than by the order of the pie slices, which helps Coherence and Cohesion.

sentences.text: Gas rose from 22 per cent to 30 per cent between 1995 and 2005, then edged up to 31 per cent in 2020.
sentences.why: Selects the main change within the stable group and reports it accurately. "Rose" and "edged up" distinguish a large from a tiny movement, which shows precise Lexical Resource and correct handling of the data.

sentences.text: Nuclear power stayed within a narrow range of 14 to 16 per cent, whereas hydroelectricity slipped from 12 per cent to 10 per cent.
sentences.why: Uses a range ("14 to 16") to summarise three values without listing each, then contrasts with "whereas". Selecting and summarising like this is what separates Band 8 from a list, and it earns Task Achievement.

sentences.text: In 2020, gas therefore ranked second behind renewables, while coal had become the smallest source.
sentences.why: Closes with the final ranking, which both pies and overview support. "Therefore" is fair because the figures justify the rank, and "while" adds a last contrast. This completes Task Achievement without needing a conclusion.

analysis: The instruction is to select and report the main features and make comparisons. With three pies and five slices each you have 15 values; reporting all of them one by one is a list, not a summary.
The pies are about share, not amount: every pie totals 100 per cent, so a source can lose share even if its output rose. Say "proportion" or "share", never "number".

Paraphrase: "pie charts show" becomes compare or illustrate; "proportion of electricity generated" becomes the share of electricity produced; "sources" can become energy sources or means of generation.
Key features to select: coal falls from 48 to 9 per cent; renewables rise from 3 to 36 per cent and take first place; gas grows moderately; nuclear and hydroelectric power barely change.

Group by pattern of change, not by pie: Body 1 for the two sources that moved dramatically, Body 2 for the three that stayed relatively stable. Use past tenses throughout because all three dates are in the past.
The question does not ask why the energy mix changed. Do not mention climate policy, cost or technology; report only what the pies show.

plan.idea: Paraphrase only: the charts compare the share of electricity Danmoor produced from five sources in 1995, 2005 and 2020. No figures.
Coal went from dominant to minor while renewables did the reverse; the other three sources were far more stable. No numbers.
Coal 48 to 36 to 9 per cent; renewables 3 to 7 to 36 per cent. Renewables replaced coal as the largest source by 2020.
Gas 22 to 30 to 31 per cent; nuclear within 14 to 16 per cent; hydroelectric 12 to 10 per cent. Final ranking in 2020: gas second, coal smallest.
